svg.text: How Kaya works, at a glance
Learn from open data, build five AI models fusing a wearable stream with the record, make them trustworthy, then put them in people's hands.
Open + synthetic data only · Decision support
real labs and liver scans ²
try a change on the twin first
the detail behind each icon above
Real glucose, meals and Fitbit data from 34 people.
4,745 adults with FibroScan liver labels; 4,827 for kidney.
Retina photographs: APTOS for training, Indian IDRiD for testing.
Our generators + simglucose: 2,000 patients; a coupled 28-day cohort links sleep, HRV and glucose.
GRU (PyTorch) + LightGBM ensemble, conformal 80% bands, isotonic-calibrated alerts.
RMSE 12.6 / 21.1 / 28.2 mg/dL at 30 / 60 / 120 min; catches 72% of lows, 45 min ahead.
LightGBM + logistic regression, explained with SHAP.
AUROC: liver 0.83 (standard FIB-4: 0.63), kidney 0.85. 1.0 is perfect, 0.5 a coin flip.
EfficientNet-B2 (timm), grades 0-4, Grad-CAM heat-maps. Kappa 0.89 on APTOS, 0.71 on IDRiD.
Eye progression and the 5-year kidney path are simulations.
Voice and documents (Sarvam AI, server-side only)
saaras:v4 speech-to-text, sarvam-105b-conversations chat, bulbul:v4-flash text-to-speech.
Sarvam Document AI reads uploaded reports. Emergency and dose rules run in code, before the model.
Wearable week (LightGBM) + record (logistic), combined by a stacker. AUROC 0.82; catches 71% of
cardiovascular events a median 22 h ahead at about 1 false alert per patient-month. Synthetic data.
Live mode runs the GRU in pure NumPy: about 1 ms per reading, no GPU.
Not built yet: consent records, a persistent audit log, ABDM. Not clinically validated.
Kaya is decision support for clinicians, not a diagnostic device.
Team Kaya · IIT Hyderabad · Digital Twin Challenge, Phase 1
